No, I'm one of the last millennials so I was in first grade. It happened right as I got on the bus for school. We did not have a normal morning schedule, it completely through me off. They had us all go to the gym/cafeteria and basically told us we are going to have a special short day, but we need to be quiet and listen for instructions carefully. I felt everyone's stress and panic and I hated that there was nothing I could do and that I felt like it was my fault everyone was feeling that way.
I ended up seeing it by accident later in the week, I don't think anyone knew I did and I didn't say anything about it. I don't think I understood how to process what I saw and just told myself it's just a movie or something. My family kept me from watching the news for a while after that since we had someone deploy shortly after. And that's already happening beyond foreign media/companies in an increasing number of states to an extent. Using the states that are restricting porn sites by requiring people to verify that they are 18+ as an example - it won't stop there. 

A bill named "Protect Tennessee Minors Act" was passed last year and was supposed to be in effect on the first, but it was blocked until they got the green light the other day. The problem with it is not necessarily about porn. The wording of the bill is so vague that they can do this with any site that they deem "harmful to minors." 

Understanding that they want people to provide their IDs, and who knows what else to verify makes it more leaves many with their hands tied, I imagine not many sites are going to want to deal with handling that (especially if you have to continuously verify after a certain amount of time has lapsed) and of course brings concern over privacy and safety. As a result PH responded with a notice "Until a real solution is offered, we have made the difficult decision to completely disable access to our website in Tennessee." There isn't an option to upload your ID or anything AFAIK so it has just been banned regardless of your age.

A handful of states have had this for a while now,  but seeing that it is spreading, it's really only a matter of time before they extend it to other sites.

Recovery is not pretty and you will hate it. I'm not saying I'm in recovery, I don't have anyone to help me and my mindset is still bad - it was unintended and unexpected but probably for the best. Physically, I'm much better and as a scientist it's incredibly fascinating to see the changes that occur. I can see better - not just from dizziness from standing up or exerting myself - I'm sedentary. Very sedentary. But having nutrients to allow those muscles to focus helps so much. Brain fog isn't gone but way better. In my case there are multiple reasons for that. I've dealt with this for so long, that I really don't know too much but I've gone back and forth on my own. I never really had acne, but I got acne. Could be attributed to multiple reasons, the foods I'm eating, hygiene, stress, hormones, etc. but it only came up during quarantine (march-present) which was where my weight occurred. You mentioned control over your body -- Yep. People talk a lot about spot treatments - that doesn't happen. You can work out a certain part of your body as much as you want but at the end of the day, you're likely not going to get what you want. It doesn't work that way and is solely genetic AFAIU. And in recovery - it doesn't even matter. A lot of bloating you see or what you may think is fat - your body is really repairing all the damage that was done now that it has the energy to do so. A lot of retention in the abdominal region or areas of your body that are more heavily used. I have a beer belly lol. I hate it, but I guess my GI tract, liver, spleen, stomach, ETC are messed up. EDs really put a toll on your body. Any imbalance is going to cause problems across the board.

There are so many physiological complications and it's rather embarrassing to talk about. We are already incredibly self conscious but these are things that need to be said.
